args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the latest deploy, checkout-api v2.3.1 failed health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an 18% error rate. v2.3.1 was also unhealthy in staging (as v2.3.1-rc). checkout-api was rolled back in all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, the service is healthy in all regions with a 0.2% error rate. Next steps: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure before redeploying, and look into why a release that was unhealthy in staging was promoted to production.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened a SEV2 incident, which paged on-call.

- **Problem:** The latest release, v2.3.1, was failing health checks in us-east, us-west and eu-west, with an 18% error rate.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. It's now running in all three regions, and the error rate has dropped to 0.2%. No approval was needed because v2.3.0 had already been healthy in production.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 (SEV2, checkout-api) describes the failure, the rollback and the result after it.

v2.3.1 had also failed in staging as v2.3.1-rc but was still released to production. I noted this in the incident and said the cause of the failure should be found before v2.3.1 is deployed again.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
